author: KC Reporter
title: Indian national pleads guilty to multimillion-dollar illegal gambling conspiracy in Missouri
text:
Tushar R. Patel, a 40-year-old Indian national residing in Georgia, pleaded guilty on May 27 in federal court for his role in a multimillion-dollar illegal gambling conspiracy that operated at six locations in southwest Missouri.
Patel entered his plea before U.S. Chief Magistrate Judge Willie J. Epps, Jr., admitting to one count each of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to operate an illegal gambling business, and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The prosecution is part of ongoing federal efforts against fraud under President Donald Trump’s administration and the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.
According to court documents, Patel and his co-conspirators obtained approximately $9.5 million through their wire fraud scheme and illegal gambling businesses from July 1, 2022, through May 13, 2025. Patel admitted that he and others ran illegal gambling operations disguised as internet amusement arcade games, skill game arcades, and adult arcades at four separate locations. These businesses employed local workers and offered contests of chance using gambling devices and slot machines in violation of state and federal law.
On May 14, 2025, Patel was charged along with eight other individuals by a federal grand jury in Springfield with multiple counts including conspiracy to commit wire fraud and operating illegal gambling businesses. Eight defendants were also charged with money laundering.
Under federal statutes, Patel faces potential sentences of up to twenty years for wire fraud conspiracy, five years for operating an illegal gambling business conspiracy, and twenty years for money laundering conspiracy without parole. Sentencing will be determined by the court following a presentence investigation by the United States Probation Office.
The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Casey Clark following investigations involving several agencies including Homeland Security Investigations; Federal Bureau of Investigation; IRS-Criminal Investigations; local police departments; state highway patrol; county prosecutors; Missouri National Guard Counter Drug Unit; Mid-States Organized Crime Information Center; Greene County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office; Jasper County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office; Johnson County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office.
The Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division on April 7 as part of broader efforts led by President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud aimed at investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against Americans.
The U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri supports community outreach programs addressing issues such as violent crime and drug trafficking while collaborating with law enforcement partners across its jurisdiction covering sixty-six counties from Iowa to Arkansas borders, according to the official website .
